overview: Two types of white blood cells (granulocytes) specialised for different threats — bacteria versus parasites and allergens.
genZNote: Neutrophils: the first responders to bacterial invasions. Eosinophils: the specialists called in for parasites and allergy drama.

aspects.label: Primary Target
aspects.valueA: Bacteria and fungi — phagocytoses and destroys them.
aspects.valueB: Multicellular parasites (like helminths) and involved in allergic reactions.

aspects.label: Relative Abundance in Blood
aspects.valueA: Most abundant white blood cell (about 50-70% of WBCs).

aspects.label: Staining Behaviour
aspects.valueA: Stains poorly with acidic or basic dyes (neutral).
aspects.valueB: Stains strongly with the acidic dye eosin (pink/red).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: A raised eosinophil count (eosinophilia) is a classic clinical clue pointing toward a parasitic infection or allergic condition.
overlay.memoryTrick: Neutrophils = neutral staining, bacteria-fighters. Eosinophils = eosin-loving, parasite-fighters.
overlay.commonMisconception: Neutrophils are not lymphocytes — they belong to the granulocyte family and work through phagocytosis, not antibody production.
